gaps.sentence: ___ the fact that the road was icy, the bus kept its usual speed.
gaps.explanation: 'Despite the fact that + clause' concedes a full clause after a preposition.

gaps.sentence: In Sweden the shops close early, ___ in Spain they stay open until ten.
gaps.explanation: 'Whereas' contrasts parallel facts about two countries.

gaps.sentence: I enjoyed the film; the ending was weak, ___.
gaps.explanation: 'Though' can come at the end of a sentence as a casual contrast marker; the others cannot.

gaps.sentence: He was warned repeatedly; ___, he ignored every safety rule.
gaps.explanation: He ignored the warnings despite receiving them: nevertheless marks that contrast.

gaps.sentence: The flight was delayed ___ thick fog.
gaps.explanation: 'Because of' + noun phrase gives the cause; although/despite express contrast.

gaps.sentence: I can't afford a holiday this year; ___, I can't get the time off work.
gaps.explanation: 'Besides' adds a further, often decisive, reason in informal style.

gaps.sentence: The negotiations dragged on for months, but they ___ collapsed.
gaps.explanation: 'Eventually' signals the outcome after much delay.

gaps.sentence: He lowered his voice ___ wake the baby.
gaps.explanation: Negative purpose = so as not to / in order not to + infinitive.
